scope: Native integer and Unicode segment writer dependencies; no bs_create_bin or other instruction admission.
adaptations: fmt_small_be/le, fmt_big_be/le, SUBc, restore_and_shift, erts_bs_put_integer_be/le and erts_bs_put_utf8/16 retain native truncation, sign extension, little-endian short-byte grouping and scalar encoding algorithms. UTF-32 retains the instruction's scalar check followed by fixed-size integer writing.

Explicit caller-owned initialized byte span and bit cursor replace ErlBitsState's implicit scheduler/register-array buffer. The caller's writer borrows its output span. No allocation, GC, ownership transfer, input-term retention, writable Binary state or process-global buffer is introduced.

Checked state/capacity/endianness/type boundaries precede all writes. Output must not overlap writer control storage; nonempty integer writes also refuse overlap with bignum input storage. Range, badarg and invalid-state refusals preserve cursor and bytes. Valid owned input terms and declared pointer spans remain caller obligations.

Descending byte stores use bounded indices instead of forming one-before-buffer pointers. FMT_COPY_VAL's unrolling is collapsed to the same arithmetic-shift byte loop. Negative signed left shifts use unsigned magnitude bits; limb counters are unsigned and restore_and_shift asserts the non-underflowing relation directly.

The integer boundary saves/restores unconsumed bits in the last partial byte, strengthening the native append-only buffer contract without changing emitted segment bits. Initialized output storage is required.

UTF copies a temporary only for a nonzero intra-byte offset. The original bin_offset condition redundantly copied an already-written aligned destination onto itself at nonzero byte offsets; that memcpy overlap is removed. Unaligned temporaries use the checked native forward bit copier.

Tests exercise compiler SUBc and its DEBUG fallback separately, independent bit and unsigned-128 oracles, maximum native bignums, Unicode scalar decoding, exact-end guard pages, and stock-OTP reference vectors. None admits the whole binary-construction case while float, append/writable, sizing, fixup and error-context dependencies remain missing.
